(1) lifestyle — wrist rest, neutral wrist, breaks · (2) night splint · (3) steroid injection (some surgeons — reduces swelling, not a cure) · (4) carpal tunnel decompression — the only definitive treatment.

a splint controls symptoms; it doesn't treat the compression — judge it after a 3-week trial; if lifestyle + splint fail → surgery. Compression never resolves by itself — it stabilises or worsens. Intermittent symptoms that settle with rest → conservative; constant, persistent symptoms → decompression.
prevent further deterioration and give the nerve a chance to recover. In very chronic severe cases recovery may be incomplete — manage expectations.
